jurisdiction: Netherlands / United Kingdom-facing platform decisions / European Union data law

observations.statement: The appellate record treated specified fraud, account-removal, allocation, pricing, and score outputs as significant automated decisions.
The public record makes a fraud-probability score and associated account-removal logic addressable.
The court release records that drivers were not heard before unilateral account removals in the described matters.
Drivers pursued the cases with support from a worker organisation, preserving collective rather than purely individual counterpower.
The court ordered the companies to provide factors, reasons, and information needed to understand and contest the decisions.
The cited public record does not establish complete account restoration, compensation, model revision, or durable compliance.

title: Uber and Ola automated-decision explanation litigation
